chunks: As for what Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā narrated from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ḥamzah, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, he said:
I asked him about the urine of a weaned boy that falls into the well, so he said: one bucket. I said: the urine of a man? He said: forty buckets are to be drawn from it.
So this does not contradict the first report, because it is possible that it be understood as referring to the urine of a boy who had not eaten food.

key_terms.أَرْبَعُونَ دَلْوًا: forty buckets, the required amount in the second case
key_terms.الصَّبِيِّ: young boy, whose urine is treated differently in the report
key_terms.الطَّعَامَ: food, used to distinguish between types of child urine in reconciling reports
key_terms.الْبِئْرِ: well, the body of water affected by impurity
key_terms.الْفَطِيمِ: weaned, describing the child in this specific case
key_terms.بَوْلِ: urine, the impurity under discussion in the ruling
key_terms.دَلْوٌ وَاحِدٌ: one bucket, the amount to be drawn in the first case
key_terms.يُنْزَحُ: is to be drawn out, referring to removal of water from the well

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on well water if the urine of a child or an adult falls into it?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning the impurity of well water when urine falls into it. It distinguishes between the urine of a weaned boy and that of an adult man, while the closing note reconciles this report with an earlier one by interpreting the earlier report as concerning a boy who had not yet eaten food.
